title: Chapter 14 — The Morning After
description: Wahala FM wants an interview. Bassey wants a cut of your fame. And every girl in the house wants to know what happens to her now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Monday. South Street is still talking about Friday. Wahala FM's Ifeoma Nwankwo is at your gate with a recorder.

beats.speaker: ifeoma
beats.text: Madam Sugar. The whole of Lagos wants to know who you are. A madam who fought traffickers? Or a madam who got caught? (She clicks the recorder on.) Your version.

variants.text: Madam Sugar. NAPTIP says your name was on the bus manifest. (She clicks the recorder on.) Do you want to say anything before the court does?

options.text: Tell her everything: Warri, the house, Felix, the girls. Your real name.
Tell a good story. Make yourself the hero, whatever happened.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: (in your best chair again) Mama Sugar! Famous now! (He opens his palm.) Fame is expensive. Forty thousand. Weekly. Like a bigger church.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: His boys are at the bar again.

options.text: "Officer Grace from NAPTIP has your phone number now, Commander. She asked me for it."
options.lockedText: You have no friend in uniform

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: (standing up very fast for a big man) Mama Sugar, we are friends, now? Old friends. (He leaves without his envelope. For the first time in eleven years.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evening. The girls, around the bar, shoes off. Nobody made Indomie. Everybody is waiting for you to say what happens now.

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: (a text) Mummy. Grandma called from Warri. She said come home, both of us, and "leave Lagos to Lagos". I'm just telling you.

beats.speaker: kemi
beats.text: Mama. Whatever you decide about the house, we want to know before Chief Dapo does.

options.text: "Each of you will choose. Stay and work the bar and kitchen, or go and start something. I'll help whoever goes."
"Tomorrow we start turning the rooms into real hotel rooms. Receipts. Locks on the inside."
"We are going home to Warri. All of it, behind us."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Tari says she wants to go home to Edo. It's the first time she has ever said where she's from. Everybody cries, including Kokoro, who says it's pepper.

beats.title: The Morning After
beats.summary: The city has a version of you now. So do the girls. Only one of them is yours to write.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You give Kokoro the keys. You give Kemi the books. You give Blessing the good mirror. You and Ivie take the night bus to Warri with two bags, which is one more than you came with.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Your mother is waiting at the motor park in Warri with a cooler of starch and banga. She has not seen you in eleven years. She says, "You are late," and then she doesn't let go.

beats.title: Back to Warri
beats.summary: You left Lagos to Lagos. It doesn't notice. Your mother does.

beats.speaker: kokoro
beats.text: (the only one who speaks) Warri. (He nods slowly.) Mama, if you go, go. Don't look back like Lot's wife. (He looks at the bar, the stairs, the girls.) But know that this house will be somebody else's by Christmas.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Every face at the bar is waiting.

options.text: "Then let it be somebody else's. We're going home."
"No. Not like this. We finish the month first."

beats.title: The Morning After
beats.summary: The city has a version of you now. So do the girls. Only one of them is yours to write.
